payload.title: Wake keys: one run per wake, recorded before the work starts
payload.description:
Every wake carries a key that says what it is about: `<automationId>|<subjectId>|<subjectVersion>|<what>` for a change, `<automationId>|schedule|<scheduled time>` for a timer, `<automationId>|manual|<request id>` for a person's Run now. The run record's id is derived from the key and created with a condition, so the same wake can never start a second run. The record is created as `started` before the procedure is loaded, so a crash leaves evidence. This replaces the random run id and the claim rows in the monitoring table (those are removed in the migration task). A run started by `papyrus procedures run` gets a manual key.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The same wake delivered twice produces one run record and one run.
- The run record exists with status `started` before any procedure code runs.
- A manual run and a scheduled run of the same agent have different keys and both run.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- wake-keys.feature: the same change delivered twice runs once; a redelivered timer runs once; two different versions of one Story run once each; a manual run has its own key; the record is `started` before the procedure loads.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None beyond A1 (the id is data). Runner image.

**Part of:** Wake contract and run outcomes. Slice code A2 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
